name: Text scramble decode

source.description: An inspected brand reel (batch 1, 2026-11-26) resolves a bracketed word out of random cycling glyphs.

technique: Each character slot cycles through random glyphs and locks to its final letter, slot by slot (usually left to right), so the word 'decodes' into place.
purpose: Signal computation, discovery or 'making sense'; a lively entrance for short technical words.
visual_behaviour: Bracketed slots flicker with symbols and letters in the accent colour; within about 0.4 s they lock into the word, which turns to the body colour.
mechanics: Split the word into character slots of fixed width (monospace avoids reflow); for each frame before a slot's lock time, pick a glyph from a charset with a seeded PRNG keyed by (slot, frame index), so any seek shows the same glyph; lock times staggered 30-60 ms per slot; colour accent -> body on lock.

decomposition.timing: 0.3-0.6 s total; 30-60 ms stagger per character; glyph change every 1-2 frames.

failure_modes: Math.random or time-based glyph picks break deterministic renders
Proportional fonts make the word jitter in width
Long scrambles on long words read as noise; keep words short

implementation.approach: Studio.type.scramble(tl, el, at, {charset, lead, stagger, step, seed, settle}) (runtime 1.17.0): each character becomes a slot holding its final letter and prebuilt glyph spans picked by Studio.rng(seed, text); the timeline switches one glyph per `step` (2 frames) until the slot's lock time (lead + slot * stagger), then shows the letter in the accent and settles it to the text colour. No callbacks, so every seek shows the same glyphs; aria-label keeps the word.

evidence.notes: Contact sheet inspected: accent glyphs cycle (0.33-0.60 s), lock left to right (DECODL at 0.73 s), settle to ink by 1.0 s. 0 errors, 0 warnings.

provenance.observed: Random glyphs in the violet accent flicker inside brackets (R, 9K, s<V, sBD) and resolve into the word within about 0.4 s.
Reverse use: the struck word's letters cycle through random glyphs for 0.7 s (5.20-5.90 s) and decay to nothing instead of locking to a word.
